what_it_does: When an AI language model generates text one word at a time (the decode phase), its main bottleneck is reading data from memory fast enough — not raw computation speed. Processing-in-memory (PIM) chips tackle this by placing simple arithmetic units directly inside the memory chip so data never has to travel across a slow bus to reach the processor. However, moving model data into PIM-friendly layouts is tricky: existing approaches fragment the data across memory channels in ways that limit how long a conversation context the model can handle and waste memory capacity. BlockPIM proposes a cross-channel block layout that arranges data across multiple independent memory channels more efficiently, removes the practical limit on context length, and redesigns the attention computation (the core operation where the model weighs how relevant each past word is to the current word) to work naturally with that distributed layout.
